versions.short: The bill would create a new federal crime covering robbery and related offenses involving automated teller machines (ATMs). It would set penalties of up to 20 years in prison for taking or attempting to take money or property from a person using or servicing an ATM, or from someone transporting cash to load into one, when done by force, violence, intimidation, or extortion. It would punish breaking into, tampering with, damaging, or stealing an ATM and taking money from it, with up to 10 years in prison for amounts over $1,000 and up to 1 year for amounts not exceeding $1,000. It would also make receiving, concealing, or selling property taken in such thefts punishable under the same penalties as the thief, and set up to 25 years in prison for assaulting someone or endangering their life with a dangerous weapon during these offenses. Finally, it would allow up to 30 years in prison, or a term of years or life if death results, for killing someone or forcing a person to accompany the offender during these crimes or while trying to avoid arrest for them.
